CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is an 18-year-old female presenting with facial acne that began approximately two years ago and is present most days. She has been using over-the-counter persa-gel and regular face washing, which she reports is somewhat helpful. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Patient reports no flare of acne with menses and states today is a good day for her acne. Mother notes that the biggest flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall, likely related to increased sweating. Current skin care routine includes: morning—washing face with water and washcloth, occasionally using elf super clarity cleanser if face feels greasy; evening—elf super clarity cleanser, toner, and persa-gel. Chest and back acne is not significant. Mother reports patient has been diligent with facial care regimen, but it has not been as effective as desired.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Denies acne flares with menses. Reports regular menstrual periods for approximately two years.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history

MEDICATIONS
Over-the-counter persa-gel, elf super clarity cleanser, toner, sunscreen SPF 30

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
No significant family history noted

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Has pets including a dog, bird, and bunnies. In 7th grade. Plays basketball, volleyball, and tap dance. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full examination performed except under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules and open and closed comedones noted. Erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Mild to moderate acne, predominantly comedonal with small inflammatory component

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate facial acne with predominantly comedonal morphology and minimal inflammatory component. Initiated topical acne therapy. Morning regimen: wash face with mild cleanser followed by noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher sunscreen. Evening regimen: wash with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to affected areas starting with a few nights per week and gradually increasing to nightly use; if cost-prohibitive or insurance coverage issues, may substitute with over-the-counter gel alternative; follow with thin layer of clean and clear persa-gel and noncomedogenic moisturizer. Counseled on potential side effects including skin sensitivity, dryness, and irritation, and emphasized importance of daily sunscreen use. Noted multiple benign moles on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with no worrisome features. Follow-up appointment scheduled in six months to assess progress. Patient instructed to call office with any questions or concerns prior to follow-up visit.
